c.tagline: Mozart's baroque city beneath a clifftop fortress, wrapped in Alpine scenery.

taxi.fareNote: Metered; taxis are picked up at ranks or booked by phone/app rather than hailed. Uber operates only on a limited basis, so licensed local taxis are the norm.

emergency.note: EU emergency 112 also works and connects to all services.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Pickpockets work the packed Getreidegasse and old-town lanes during festival season and Christmas markets.

hood_desc: The baroque UNESCO heart on the left bank, a warren of narrow lanes and squares below Hohensalzburg Fortress, taking in Getreidegasse, Mozart's Birthplace, the cathedral and the finest hotels; the classic, if priciest, place to stay.

The 'new town' on the right bank around Mirabell Palace and its gardens, with Mozart's Residence, the Kapuzinerberg and the Linzergasse shopping street; central and slightly better value, with many of the city's larger historic hotels.
A quiet, green residential quarter tucked below Nonnberg Abbey and the fortress just south of the old town; leafy and calm, good for families and longer stays while still walkable to the centre.
A peaceful residential area west of the old town, home to Schloss Leopoldskron of Sound of Music fame; low-key and local with easy access to the centre on foot, by bus or by bike.

The practical district around the main railway station, with the best transport links and the city's budget hotels and hostels; handy for day trips by train and a short walk or bus ride from the sights.
lodging: Hotel Goldener Hirsch, a Luxury Collection Hotel

water.note: Alpine tap water is excellent and safe to drink.

transit.pay: Salzburg's network is run by Salzburg AG (Obus trolleybuses and city buses) within the SVV tariff; buy a single ticket (about €2.20, cheaper in advance from machines, Tabak-Trafik shops or the app) or a 24-hour ticket (around €4.60) and validate on board. The regional S-Bahn uses the same tariff.
transit.hours: Obus and bus lines run roughly 5:30am to 11:30pm, with BusStar night buses on Friday, Saturday and before holidays covering the small hours.
transit.note: Salzburg has no metro or tram; the electric Obus trolleybus network is the backbone of city transport, supplemented by diesel buses and the S-Bahn suburban trains.

transit.m: Obus trolleybus line 2 to Salzburg Hauptbahnhof, ~20-25 min
Obus trolleybus line 10 to the Old Town (Rathaus), ~15-20 min

places.note: claims to be Europe's oldest restaurant, in the abbey since 803; the grand-setting version

landmarks: Hohensalzburg Fortress
This massive medieval fortress crowns the city on Festungsberg hill and is one of the largest surviving castles in Europe, offering iconic views over Salzburg's old town.
Mirabell Palace and Gardens
These baroque gardens, famous from 'The Sound of Music,' feature manicured flowerbeds, statues, and a postcard-perfect view of the fortress beyond.
Salzburg Cathedral (Salzburger Dom)
This magnificent baroque cathedral with twin towers dominates the old town skyline and is the spiritual heart of Salzburg.
Getreidegasse
A charming pedestrian shopping street lined with wrought-iron guild signs and the birthplace of Mozart, capturing old-world Salzburg atmosphere.
Mozart's Birthplace
The bright yellow house where Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart was born in 1756 is now a museum and one of the city's most visited sites.
Residenzplatz
A grand baroque square at the heart of the old town, anchored by an ornate fountain and surrounded by historic prince-archbishop buildings.
Hellbrunn Palace
A whimsical 17th-century palace famous for its trick fountains and expansive gardens, a favorite day-trip destination just south of the city.
Makartsteg Bridge
This pedestrian bridge over the Salzach River, covered in love locks, frames a classic view of the old town and fortress skyline.
Nonnberg Abbey
A centuries-old Benedictine convent perched above the city, notable both for its history and its role as inspiration in 'The Sound of Music.'
Untersberg
A dramatic mountain on the city's outskirts, reached by cable car, offering breathtaking alpine panoramas over Salzburg and the surrounding Alps.

intl.op: ÖBB / SBB railjet via the Arlberg Pass

train.note: Everything runs from Salzburg Hauptbahnhof, about 15 minutes' walk or a short bus ride north of the old town, and it is an unusually good sleeper hub for a city of this size. Check days of running before booking: the Brussels Nightjet goes only on Tuesdays, Thursdays and Sundays, while the Vienna-Venice Nightjet passes through Salzburg at around 2am even though it is bookable from here. Booking normally opens six months ahead for ÖBB services but only about 90 days ahead for the Polish EuroNight sleepers Chopin and Carpatia, which leave together at 20:30 and split later. There is no direct train to Prague - change at Linz, roughly 5h25 in total - and on the Vienna and Innsbruck corridors the open-access operator WESTbahn competes with ÖBB, so compare both.

intl.to: Munich, Vienna, Prague, Ljubljana & across Europe

bus.note: There is no separate coach station: international and long-distance buses use the stops on Sudtiroler Platz right outside Salzburg Hauptbahnhof, so train and bus connections are easy. FlixBus is the main international operator, with Munich about 2 hours away and Vienna around 3h30 - cheaper than the train but slower, and worth booking online in advance. For the surrounding Salzkammergut, ÖBB Postbus (https://www.postbus.at/en) runs the regional network from the same forecourt, including the popular route 150 to St Gilgen on the Wolfgangsee and on to Bad Ischl. Austria is in Schengen, so there are no routine border checks toward Germany, though spot checks do happen.

ferry.note: Salzburg is landlocked; the only boats are Salzach river sightseeing cruises in the city and seasonal lake steamers on the nearby Wolfgangsee, Konigssee and Hallstattersee, none of which are transport links to anywhere else.

half.name: Berchtesgaden
half.blurb: A German alpine town about 30 minutes away sits below the Eagle's Nest teahouse and the turquoise waters of Lake Königssee.

half.name: Werfen
half.blurb: A castle town about 40 minutes south has the medieval Hohenwerfen fortress and the Eisriesenwelt ice caves carved into the mountainside above it.

half.name: St. Gilgen
half.blurb: A lakeside village about 30 minutes away on the Wolfgangsee was the birthplace of Mozart's mother and is reached along a scenic lake road.

half.name: Hallstatt
half.blurb: A lakeside village about an hour and 20 minutes away has pastel houses stacked against a mountainside above the Hallstättersee, with an ancient salt mine above town.
